data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 10 observations; candidates: unknown

observations.finding: Fields f_7e75dff6926a and f_67c8c8380ec0 less confluent than DMSO f_9fbcadfb9d0d with more intercellular gaps and fewer nuclei per FOV. Occasional very large flattened cells especially at bottom-right f_7e75 and lower-left f_67c8c8380ec0.
Reduced cell number / anti-proliferative. Visual sparsity is modest but consistent with measured cell_count z=-4.578 (227.5 vs DMSO median 311.5).
Increased cell size: cytoplasm (red actin cortex + green tubulin) more spread, elongated. Large cells ~40% larger area average.

cell_area strongly increased: z=+9.55 (4682 vs 3315.5) and cell_major_axis z=+6.16 (105.7 vs 88.9) visible as larger, more elongated cell footprints. No separate gray channel, read from red+green extent in composite.
Nuclei (blue DNA) enlarged and slightly more elongated oval: nuc_area z=+5.95 (973 vs 792) and nuc_major_axis z=+4.01 (39.8 vs 36.5) visible. Heterogeneous, some polyploid-like very large nuclei.

Apparent increase in DNA content: nuclei on average bluer/brighter and larger. Hard to quantify integrated intensity by eye in composite without grayscale, but consistent with nuc_dna_integrated z=+4.59 (406.6 vs 291.9) indicating G2/M arrest/polyploidy.
Nuclear shape largely regular, smooth border, round to oval, no frequent multilobation, micronuclei or fragmentation. Slightly more solid.

nuc_solidity z=+5.67 (0.974 vs 0.972) very small absolute change but statistically strong - visual solidity unchanged to slightly more convex. nuc_form_factor z=-2.88 (0.912 vs 0.917, |z|<3 not strong) - slight elongation without irregularity, matching visual impression.

beta-tubulin (green) filamentous network intact, no depolymerization, no strong bundles/asters. F-actin (red) cortical staining retained, no loss of stress fibers, no punctate actin aggregates. Few bright white-yellow mitotic figures in both treated and DMSO, no obvious mitotic arrest rosettes.

Microtubule and actin phenotypes: no Actin disruptor, Microtubule destabilizer or stabilizer, Eg5 inhibitor characteristic patterns visible in green/red composite. NOT covered by provided measurements (no tubulin/actin features in top_deviations).

notable_cells.why: bright yellow-white mitotic/apoptotic cell with condensed blue DNA + green tubulin colocalization
very large flattened cell with enlarged round nucleus, example of increased cell_area/nuc_area phenotype
very large cell with large nucleus, left edge, exemplifies hypertrophy

candidate_mechanisms.why: Visible hypertrophy with enlarged nuclei, increased DNA content and reduced count indicates cell-cycle arrest / polyploidy. Pattern overlaps DNA damage, DNA replication, Aurora kinase inhibitors, Kinase inhibitors and others on list. With only composites (no grayscale) and intact actin/tubulin, cannot distinguish; no definitive actin/microtubule or Aurora multilobation phenotype to assign one class. Do not guess compound.

report.uncertainty: Only composites at identical contrast, 24h MCF-7. Subtle intensity/shape calls limited without grayscale. Do not guess compound.

data.rationale: Visual check of high-dose phenotype vs DMSO

data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 5 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, unknown

observations.finding: Markedly lower cell density in both treated fields (f_9b9f012410a1, f_4d4621ad2e67) vs DMSO f_9fbcadfb9d0d: large black cell-free areas, estimated ~60-70% fewer nuclei, no confluent monolayer.
Higher F-actin (red) contrast and variance: more prominent bright peripheral stress fibers / ruffled edges and increased overall red intensity vs thin cortical actin in dense DMSO.
Higher beta-tubulin (green) contrast and variance: brighter, more distinct filament bundles in isolated spread cells vs more uniform dim green network in DMSO.

Nuclei (blue/DAPI) fewer, on average larger and less round vs DMSO oval uniform nuclei; several bi-nucleated / enlarged irregular nuclei and indentations. Blue signal appears fainter per-field only because of sparsity, not quantified.

Cells more isolated and spread with spiky / stellate edges; occasional enlarged cells, failed cytokinesis pairs and thin intercellular bridges (visible green tubulin tether) vs tightly packed epithelial sheet in DMSO.

notable_cells.why: spread cell with elongated green tether between two small islands, example of increased tubulin contrast and lower density
cluster with multiple enlarged irregular nuclei example of reduced form_factor/solidity

candidate_mechanisms.why: best fit to combination of strong reduction in cell count, decreased nuc_form_factor and solidity (irregular enlarged/polyploid nuclei, bi-nucleation, failed cytokinesis) with retained/enhanced microtubule and actin filaments in large spread cells; classic Aurora cytokinesis-failure phenotype

Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers also increase tubulin variance/contrast and can cause mitotic defects and irregular nuclei, but no clear microtubule loss/bundling pathognomonic pattern can be concluded from composite only; actin disruptor, DNA damage/replication, Eg5 patterns not supported

report.uncertainty: No separate grayscale channels provided; reading stains from RGB composite limits quantitative assessment of nuclear size/intensity. Cytoskeletal increases partly secondary to increased cell spread area from low density (~70% fewer cells) vs true polymerization change.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call is justified and calibrated. Across the three non-toxic doses (0.3, 1, 3 \u00b5M), nuclear enlargement and increased integrated DNA are concordant (nuc_area z +3.6 to +6.0), with intact actin/tubulin and no mitotic or multinucleation signal to support Aurora/Eg5/microtubule classes. Each dose is a single well, but the consistent mid-dose trend mitigates this, and the budget is exhausted (0 left) with atlas, dose-response, and phenotype analyses already performed. Compound: **cisplatin** (PubChem CID [5702198](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5702198))

Correct: agent said **DNA damage**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

Unblinded cisplatin (CHEMBL11359, DNA inhibitor) matches DNA damage call (p=0.52, verdict correct). Evidence got right: consistent enlarged nuclei/cell hypertrophy across non-toxic doses e2 nuc_area z+5.8/cell_area z+4.1, e6 cell_area z+9.6/nuc_area z+6.0, e5 cell_area z+3.8/nuc_area z+3.6 with intact actin/tubulin and e12 frac_large_nucleus rho+0.80 and e7 atlas NSC 2/4 DNA damage (6/10 neighbors) vs DNA replication 1/4 (3/10). Acquisition choice to sample mid-dose (e2) then high-dose (e3) then fill low-mid gap (e5,e6) and re-compare (e7) was why trajectory corrected. No clinical implications.
